title: Type switches
hints: A type switch, `switch x := v.(type) { case int: … }`, branches on the dynamic type stored in an `any` value. Inside each case, x has that case's type.
fmt.Sprintf with %d, %q (a quoted string) and %t (a bool) produces the exact formats. `case nil:` matches a nil interface value.

switch x := v.(type) { case nil: "nil"; case int: fmt.Sprintf("int %d", x); case string: fmt.Sprintf("string %q", x); case bool: fmt.Sprintf("bool %t", x); case []int: fmt.Sprintf("[]int of length %d", len(x)); default: "unknown" }
